def: Uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation that dissipates the proton gradient, so energy is released as heat instead of ATP. Used illicitly for weight loss; causes hyperthermia and death.
Cardiac arrest with organized electrical activity on the ECG but no palpable pulse. Treated with CPR and epinephrine, and by finding the cause (the Hs and Ts).
Inhaled anticholinergic bronchodilator, such as ipratropium, used with beta agonists in acute asthma or COPD exacerbations.
Gene encoding fibrocystin; mutated in autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease, which causes enlarged cystic kidneys in infants and can cause Potter sequence.
Segment of the loop of Henle that reabsorbs sodium, potassium and chloride via NKCC2 without water. Site of action of loop diuretics.
Pyrimidine nucleotide made de novo by orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase; elevated orotic acid results from defects here.
Universal methyl donor formed from methionine and ATP. Used for methylation of DNA, proteins and neurotransmitters.
Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells, causing achlorhydria and loss of intrinsic factor. Leads to pernicious anemia.
Variant hemoglobin with lysine replacing glutamate in the beta chain. Causes mild hemolytic anemia with target cells and crystals.
GPI-anchored protein (CD55) on blood cells that prevents complement activation. Absent in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.
Antibody-mediated destruction of red blood cells. Warm type is IgG and associated with lupus; cold type is IgM, associated with Mycoplasma and EBV.
Division of the nervous system controlling involuntary functions, comprising sympathetic and parasympathetic branches.
Thalamic nucleus relaying body sensation from the spinothalamic and dorsal column pathways to the somatosensory cortex.
DNA polymerase adding random nucleotides to developing lymphocyte receptor genes. Marker of immature lymphoblasts in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Surface marker on T cells and on a subset of B cells. Positive in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and mantle cell lymphoma.
The alpha chain of the IL-2 receptor, found on activated T cells and regulatory T cells. Positive on hairy cell leukemia.
Tyrosine kinase gene on chromosome 9. In chronic myeloid leukemia, it fuses with BCR on chromosome 22 to form constitutively active BCR-ABL.
Membrane protein on chromosome 21 cleaved to form amyloid-beta. Mutations or trisomy 21 cause early-onset Alzheimer disease.
Neurodegenerative disease with parkinsonism, autonomic failure and cerebellar signs; alpha-synuclein inclusions in glial cells.
Screening test detecting hidden blood in stool, used for colorectal cancer screening.
Brief episodes of vertigo triggered by head position, from displaced otoliths in a semicircular canal. Diagnosed by the Dix-Hallpike test; treated with Epley maneuver.
Antidepressant class, such as venlafaxine and duloxetine, that blocks reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine. Also used for neuropathic pain.
Proportion by which an intervention lowers risk compared with control: (control event rate minus treatment rate) divided by the control rate.
Fatty liver disease linked to obesity, insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome. Formerly called NAFLD.
T cell costimulatory receptor binding B7 (CD80/86) on antigen-presenting cells. Required with the TCR signal for T cell activation.
Exaggerated immune responses causing tissue damage, grouped into types I to IV.
Exfoliative toxin-mediated skin peeling in infants, with a positive Nikolsky sign. Toxin cleaves desmoglein 1.
Non-random cluster of congenital defects: vertebral, anal atresia, cardiac, tracheoesophageal fistula, renal and limb anomalies.
Fever and chills during or after transfusion, caused by recipient antibodies against donor leukocytes or cytokines. Benign and treated with antipyretics.
Succimer, an oral chelator used for lead, mercury and arsenic poisoning.
Inhaled anticholinergic bronchodilator, such as tiotropium, used for long-term COPD treatment.
Knee ligament preventing posterior displacement of the tibia on the femur. Injured in dashboard impacts; shown by posterior drawer sign.
Proto-oncogene encoding the stem cell factor receptor. Activating mutations cause gastrointestinal stromal tumors and mastocytosis.
Transcription factor that drives cell-cycle progression at G1/S. Held inactive by Rb until Rb is phosphorylated by cyclin D/CDK4.
Blood test from an artery measuring pH, PaCO2, PaO2 and bicarbonate to assess ventilation and acid-base status.
Chelating agent used for lead poisoning; also an anticoagulant in blood tubes.
RNA picornavirus transmitted fecal-orally, causing self-limited acute hepatitis without chronic disease.
Lateral hip pain from trochanteric bursitis or gluteal tendinopathy, worse lying on the affected side.
Excess bacteria in the small bowel, causing bloating, diarrhea and malabsorption (fat-soluble vitamins, B12 deficiency).
Removal of abnormal cervical tissue with a wire loop, used for high-grade cervical dysplasia.

term: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance
def: Mildly abnormal Pap smear result; managed with HPV testing or repeat cytology.
Third-trimester liver failure from microvesicular fat in hepatocytes, with hypoglycemia, coagulopathy and elevated bilirubin.

term: Men who have sex with men
def: Epidemiologic term for male-male sexual contact, used for risk assessment of sexually transmitted infections.
G-protein coupled receptor on parathyroid and kidney cells that senses calcium. Mutations cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
Hepatitis C viral serine protease required for polyprotein processing; targeted by direct-acting antivirals like glecaprevir.
Defective RNA virus requiring hepatitis B surface antigen to replicate. Causes coinfection or superinfection with HBV.
Membrane lipid cleaved by phospholipase C into IP3 and DAG in Gq signaling.
Long unbranched polysaccharides in the extracellular matrix, such as hyaluronic acid and heparan sulfate. Accumulate in Graves orbitopathy and mucopolysaccharidoses.
Urinary metabolite of serotonin; elevated in carcinoid syndrome.
VIPoma syndrome with watery diarrhea, hypokalemia and achlorhydria, caused by vasoactive intestinal peptide secretion.
Aggressive neuroendocrine lung tumor, strongly linked to smoking, that can secrete ACTH or ADH. Typically central, with L-myc amplification.
Receptor on osteoclast precursors that binds RANKL from osteoblasts, triggering osteoclast formation. Blocked by denosumab.
Unexplained death of an infant under 1 year, usually during sleep. Risk factors include prone sleeping and smoke exposure.
Removal of the first draining lymph node to assess whether cancer, such as breast cancer or melanoma, has spread.
X-linked defect of androgen receptors; 46,XY individuals with female external genitalia, undescended testes and elevated testosterone and LH.
Obstetric history shorthand: Gravidity, Term births, Preterm births, Abortions and Living children.
Start codon in mRNA that codes for methionine (formylmethionine in prokaryotes).
DNA mismatch repair gene. Mutations cause Lynch syndrome and microsatellite instability.
Lynch syndrome; autosomal dominant mismatch repair defect causing early colorectal, endometrial and other cancers.
Congenital defect where all pulmonary veins drain to the right heart instead of the left atrium, causing cyanosis.
Ultrasound of the heart through the esophagus, giving better views than transthoracic echo.
Sudden regular narrow-complex tachycardia from a reentrant circuit above the ventricles, such as AVNRT. Terminated by vagal maneuvers or adenosine.
Intracellular proteins phosphorylated by the insulin receptor that propagate signaling through PI3K and AKT.
Drugs, such as methotrexate and sulfasalazine, that slow progression of rheumatoid arthritis, unlike analgesics.
Proto-oncogene encoding a transcription factor. Translocated in Burkitt lymphoma; amplified in small cell lung cancer and neuroblastoma.
Chemokine released from platelet alpha granules that binds heparin. Antibodies to heparin-PF4 complexes cause HIT.
Rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis. Activated by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate; inhibited by ATP and citrate.
Plasma protein that inactivates thrombin and factor Xa; its action is enhanced by heparin.
Anticoagulant of mixed chain lengths, given by IV infusion, that activates antithrombin; monitored with aPTT and reversed by protamine.

term: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
def: Failure caused by impaired diastolic filling with a stiff ventricle and normal ejection fraction. Associated with hypertension, obesity and sleep apnea.
Reduced pupil response when light shines in the affected eye, seen with swinging flashlight. Indicates optic nerve or severe retinal disease.
Gene on chromosome 22 that fuses with ABL after the Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22), creating BCR-ABL in chronic myeloid leukemia.
Immunoglobulin heavy-chain gene locus on chromosome 14, translocated in lymphomas such as follicular and Burkitt lymphoma.
Lymphoid tissue in mucosal sites; MALT lymphoma is a marginal zone lymphoma linked to H. pylori.
Test separating serum proteins to detect an M spike in monoclonal gammopathy such as multiple myeloma.
Highest value of a laboratory reference range.
Asymptomatic premalignant plasma cell proliferation with M protein, below myeloma thresholds.
Cerebral artery supplying the medial frontal and parietal lobes. Occlusion causes contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss.
Fatty acids over 22 carbons, degraded in peroxisomes. They accumulate in adrenoleukodystrophy and Zellweger syndrome.
CD8 T cells that kill virus-infected and tumor cells via perforin and granzymes.
Prion disease with rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus and spongiform change. EEG shows periodic sharp waves.
Gene (deleted in colorectal cancer) whose loss contributes to colorectal cancer in the adenoma-carcinoma sequence.
Seizures arising from one area of the brain with reduced awareness, often with automatisms. Formerly complex partial seizures.
Fluid pressure inside the eye. Elevated in glaucoma.
Radiologic shunt between portal and hepatic veins to relieve portal hypertension. Can worsen hepatic encephalopathy.
Toll-like receptor that recognizes bacterial lipopolysaccharide with CD14, triggering inflammation.
Co-receptor with TLR4 for bacterial lipopolysaccharide, found on monocytes and macrophages.
Signaling complex associated with the T cell receptor; marker of all T cells.
Receptor on B cells and antigen-presenting cells that binds CD40 ligand on T cells, driving class switching. Defect causes hyper-IgM syndrome.
Proapoptotic BCL-2 family protein that forms pores in the mitochondrial membrane to release cytochrome c.
Proapoptotic BCL-2 family protein that forms mitochondrial pores to release cytochrome c, activated by p53.
Bleach-like product of myeloperoxidase in the neutrophil oxidative burst, killing phagocytosed microbes.
MHC class II allele associated with multiple sclerosis, hay fever, SLE and Goodpasture syndrome.
X-linked recessive dystrophin gene frameshift mutation causing progressive muscle weakness, Gowers sign and calf pseudohypertrophy.
Concentrate of factors II, VII, IX and X for rapid warfarin reversal.
Ectodermal thickening at the limb bud tip secreting FGF to drive limb outgrowth along the proximal-distal axis.
Mesoderm at the posterior limb bud that secretes Sonic hedgehog to pattern the anteroposterior axis.
Injury mechanism causing distal radius, scaphoid and clavicle fractures.
Phosphoinositide 3-kinase; signaling enzyme downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases that activates AKT to promote growth and survival.
Serine/threonine kinase activated by PI3K that promotes cell survival and growth.
Respiratory support with a mask providing BiPAP or CPAP without intubation.
Conjugate vaccine covering 20 pneumococcal serotypes, given to children and at-risk adults.
E. coli causing traveler's diarrhea via heat-labile and heat-stable toxins.
X-ray of the bladder and urethra during urination, used to detect vesicoureteral reflux and posterior urethral valves.
Benign infant colitis with bloody stools from cow's milk or soy protein intolerance, resolving by age 1.
Arenavirus spread by rodent excreta, causing aseptic meningitis and congenital infection.
Glucose intolerance first recognized during pregnancy, from placental hormones causing insulin resistance.
Measure of uterine contraction strength, the sum of peak pressures above baseline over 10 minutes. Over 200 is adequate labor.

term: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
def: Failure of pulmonary vascular resistance to fall after birth, causing right-to-left shunting and hypoxemia.
The most common paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, caused by a reentry circuit within the AV node.
Severe mood symptoms in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle that resolve with menses. Treated with SSRIs.
IV fluid used to treat neonatal hypoglycemia.
Severe drug reaction with epidermal detachment over 30 percent of body surface, mucosal involvement and a positive Nikolsky sign.
Gastric cells that secrete histamine under gastrin and ACh stimulation, acting on parietal cells.
Neuropeptide released by vagal stimulation that triggers gastrin release by G cells.
Hepatitis C viral protein needed for replication and assembly. Inhibited by ledipasvir and velpatasvir.
Lipid second messenger from PIP2 cleavage by phospholipase C; activates protein kinase C.
Cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase associated with cytokine receptors, phosphorylating STAT proteins. Mutated in polycythemia vera (JAK2).
Energy expenditure at rest, raised by thyroid hormone.
Cytochrome P450 enzyme metabolizing warfarin, phenytoin and sulfonylureas.
Cytosine-guanine rich DNA regions near promoters. Methylation silences gene transcription.
DNA mismatch repair gene. Mutations cause Lynch syndrome (HNPCC).
Pathway removing bulky DNA lesions like thymine dimers. Defective in xeroderma pigmentosum.
Ribonucleoprotein binding a signal sequence and bringing the ribosome to the rough ER.
Volume of blood remaining in the ventricle after ejection. Stroke volume equals EDV minus ESV.
Potassium channel gene mutated in Romano-Ward and Jervell and Lange-Nielsen long QT syndromes.
Fastidious gram-negative bacteria causing culture-negative endocarditis: Haemophilus, Aggregatibacter, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella and Kingella.
Blood tests including TSH and thyroid hormones used to assess thyroid status.
Protein domain that binds phosphorylated tyrosine, mediating signaling downstream of insulin and growth factor receptors.
Class of calcium channel blockers (amlodipine, nifedipine) acting on vascular smooth muscle.
Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours of transfusion, due to donor anti-leukocyte antibodies.
Glycolysis intermediate; phosphorylated by PFK-1 to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
Glycolysis intermediate formed from glucose by hexokinase and dephosphorylated by glucose-6-phosphatase.
Renal transporter that reabsorbs urate in the proximal tubule. Inhibited by probenecid.
Lipoxygenase product that is a potent neutrophil chemotactic factor.
About 60 percent of body weight, divided into intracellular and extracellular compartments.
Cysteine protease from group A Streptococcus. A nephritogenic antigen in poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
Antibody to streptolysin O, raised after group A streptococcal infection and elevated in rheumatic fever.
Total hemolytic complement assay measuring classical pathway function. Low in poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
Imprinted tumor suppressor locus at 11p15; abnormal expression is associated with Wilms tumor and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.
